anti_overlap: Defer calendrical-canon admission/retirement rule questions to fd-kigo-saijiki-canonical-registry.
Defer temporal volatility/basenote-vs-topnote curve shape questions to fd-parfumerie-drydown-salience-phases.
Defer tick-pipeline deterministic release cadence questions to fd-horological-escapement-tick-cadence.
decision_lens: Evaluate whether the earned-epithet pipeline models deed-witness-recitation-echo faithfully, and whether the Max-2 display cap plus linear -0.5/day decay reproduces the 'permanent-to-bearer, fading-in-colony-mouth' asymmetry that defines a living praise-name register.
distance_rationale: A pre-modern oral knowledge-system from an African linguistic tradition is structurally and culturally distant from Rust ECS game-simulation engineering.
expected_isomorphisms: The jeli/jamu separation (the griot keeps the register, the bearer carries the claim, the community sustains it through recitation) maps directly onto the ColonyLexicon/Epithets split plus salience-by-reference. The witnessed-deed attribution rule transfers to trigger-emission discipline.
focus: Verify the earned-epithet lifecycle honors the grammar of performative praise-name traditions: the name is earned by witnessed deed, carried permanently by the bearer, and kept alive in the collective tongue only through recitation.
name: fd-griot-jeliya-praise-name-salience
persona: Apply the perspective of a Mande jeli (djeli) steeped in the jeliya tradition — they care about the fidelity of the link between deed and jamu (praise-name), the discipline of recitation that keeps a name vivid, and the etiquette of when a name is spoken, suppressed, or passed; they measure whether salience reflects performance cadence rather than mere elapsed time, and they flag epithets that become mute plaques rather than living utterances.
review_areas: Does the +10 earn / +2 reference / -0.5/day curve actually degrade a never-referenced epithet into gossip-silence at roughly the right tick horizon for a colony that lacks active gossip consumers this sprint (Open Question 5), or is it too fast/slow relative to the timescale of recitation opportunity?

For the 7 canonical triggers: which ones name a WITNESSED public deed (the Defiant, Silverstring, Stormborn) versus a PRIVATE or INFERRED condition (the Quiet, the Patient, Heartmender)? Praise-name traditions require witnesses — does the emission site for the witness-less ones feel ceremonially earned, or will players perceive them as administrative tags?

Display resolution sorts by salience desc, tie-break earned_tick asc. In jeliya, the FIRST name earned often has priority regardless of current recitation — verify the tie-break direction truly represents 'older = more prestigious', and check whether a decayed-but-ancient epithet can be unjustly pushed out of the top-2 by a fresh high-salience one.

Departure farewell integration reads top epithet into narrative text. In praise-name tradition, the name spoken at leave-taking is ritually specified, not just 'top'. Does the current design risk pulling a high-salience recent epithet over a more identity-defining older one at FulfilledDeparture and ElfDeparted?

Heartmender granularity (Open Question 4): praise-name traditions almost always require that the named deed be singular and attributable. If both partners have resolved heartbreak and both earn Heartmender on the same PartnershipFormed, the name loses attribution crispness — recommend unambiguous rules.

ColonyLexicon storage keeps canonical text separate from per-elf LexemeId refs. This matches the jeli model (the colony/griot keeps the register, the person carries the claim) — but confirm there is no path where a lexeme is removed/mutated in ColonyLexicon while Epithets components still hold a dangling ref.

severity_examples.condition: Salience-only display ordering paired with no active gossip consumer creates recency-bias in ritual text.
severity_examples.scenario: An elf earns 'the Defiant' early in life, it decays to salience <= 2.0 (no gossip consumers yet), a younger elf earns 'Stormborn' at high intensity; on FulfilledDeparture the narrative pulls 'Stormborn' even though 'the Defiant' is the identity the colony remembers them by across their whole life.

severity_examples.condition: Open Question 4 is resolved permissively (one-is-enough) without a uniqueness rule on deed-attribution.
severity_examples.scenario: Heartmender fires on both partners when both have resolved scars, producing two simultaneous Heartmenders for one PartnershipFormed event. The lexicon records two entries with the same deed-anchor, fracturing the 'witnessed attribution' logic the name depends on.

severity_examples.condition: Stateful-scan triggers lack a narrative-emission hook that grounds the name in a witness act.
severity_examples.scenario: the Quiet fires at Elder stage transition for an introvert who never performed. In jeliya, a name for a person-who-did-not-speak is a contradiction unless someone ELSE spoke of them; emission feels administrative rather than witnessed.

source_domain: West African Mande jeliya tradition — jeli (griot) lineage of praise-name (jamu) custody and performance
success_hints: Ground each of the 7 triggers in a WITNESS model — who in the sim played the role of jeli, and when.
Distinguish 'salience in gossip' from 'salience in ritual naming' — the farewell text might want a separate ordering.
Audit whether a decayed epithet can lose its display slot to a newer one, and whether that matches player expectations about lifetime identity.
task_context: The brainstorm proposes earned epithets tied to a colony lexicon with linear salience decay; review through a praise-name-tradition lens to surface attribution, recitation, and ritual-invocation issues invisible from inside ECS design.
